# New-ZbxMapElement

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a map element for the -Element of New-ZbxMap and Set-ZbxMap.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxMapElement [-EvaluationType <ZabbixConditionEvaluationType>] [-Tag <ZabbixMapElementTagRequest[]>] [-MapElementId <ulong>] [-ShowLabel <ZabbixMapShowElementLabel>] [-ZIndex <int>] [-ElementType <ZabbixMapElementType>] [-IconIdOff <ulong>] [-IconIdOn <ulong>] [-Label <string>] [-LabelLocation <ZabbixMapLabelLocation>] [-X <int>] [-Y <int>] [-IconIdDisabled <ulong>] [-IconIdMaintenance <ulong>] [-ElementSubType <ZabbixMapElementSubType>] [-AreaType <ZabbixMapElementAreaType>] [-Width <int>] [-Height <int>] [-ViewType <int>] [-UseIconMap <bool>] [-Element <ZabbixMapElementElementRequest[]>] [-Url <ZabbixMapElementUrlRequest[]>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An element is one icon on a network map: a host, a host group, a trigger, another map or a plain image. The New-ZbxMapElement cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -Element of New-ZbxMap and Set-ZbxMap take as it is, alone or in an array. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build an element record

```powershell
New-ZbxMapElement -MapElementId 1 -ElementType Image -ZIndex 2
```

The builder writes a hashtable in the wire shape of one map element (selements); only the fields bound are set.

### Example 2: Bring a map's elements to the front

```powershell
$elements = (Get-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map' -SelectElements).Elements |
    ForEach-Object { New-ZbxMapElement -MapElementId $_.MapElementId -ElementType $_.ElementType -ZIndex 10 }
$null = Set-ZbxMap -InputObject 'Office map' -Element $elements
(Get-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map' -SelectElements).Elements | Format-Table MapElementId, Label, X, Y, ZIndex
```

An element with an existing -MapElementId updates that element in place, keeping its label and position; Set-ZbxMap -Element sends them all. -ZIndex (and -ShowLabel) need Zabbix 7.4 or later.
